data.stem: The Harappan Civilisation is also known by which name?
options: Indus Valley Civilisation
Vedic Civilisation of the later Rigvedic period
Maurya Civilisation
Mughal Civilisation
data.explanation: Indus Valley Civilisation is correct as the alternate name. Vedic Civilisation is wrong because it is a later culture, while Maurya and Mughal options are wrong because they belong to much later empires.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The mature phase of the Harappan Civilisation is dated to about which period?
options: 500 BCE - 500 CE
data.explanation: 2600-1900 BCE is correct for the mature phase of developed towns and standardised planning. 1500-500 BCE is wrong because it is the Vedic period, 500 BCE-500 CE is the early historic period, and 1200-1500 CE is medieval.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which site is identified as the largest known Harappan settlement in the cited PIB release?
options: Rakhigarhi
Mohenjo-Daro
Lothal
Kalibangan
data.explanation: Rakhigarhi in Haryana, at about 550 hectares, is identified as the largest known settlement. Mohenjo-Daro is wrong because it is a major, well-preserved city but smaller (NCERT: about 125 hectares); Lothal and Kalibangan are wrong because they are much smaller sites.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which statement about building material at Mohenjo-Daro is most accurate?
options: Both baked and sun-dried bricks were used
Only unbaked brick was used
Only stone slabs were used
Only timber was used
data.explanation: Both baked and sun-dried bricks is correct: NCERT records both, and UNESCO's full description calls the city mostly baked brick. 'Only unbaked brick' is wrong because baked brick is prominent in drains and baths, while stone-only and timber-only misstate the brick architecture.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Excavations at Mohenjo-Daro began in which year?
data.explanation: 1922 is correct as the excavation start. The year 1826 is wrong because it marks the Harappa identification, 1980 is wrong because it is the UNESCO year, and 1900 is wrong because it matches neither event.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Mohenjo-Daro was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in which year?
data.explanation: 1980 is correct as the inscription year. The year 1922 is wrong because it is the excavation start, 1826 is wrong because it belongs to Harappa identification, and 2000 is wrong because it does not match the inscription.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Roughly how many Harappan sites have been discovered?
options: About ten
More than a thousand
About fifty
Only two, Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro
data.explanation: More than a thousand is correct (PIB uses this count in its Dholavira release). About ten and about fifty are wrong because they understate the network, and 'only two' is wrong because it ignores sites such as Dholavira, Lothal and Rakhigarhi.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which feature shows that Mohenjo-Daro was a planned city?
options: A purely random scatter of houses
A grid layout with covered drainage and aligned streets
Absence of any public structure
Houses built without standardisation
data.explanation: A grid layout with drainage and aligned streets is correct as planning evidence. Random scatter is wrong because it denies planning, while absence of public structures and lack of standardisation are wrong because they contradict baths, drains and brick standards.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which structures are associated with Mohenjo-Daro in the cited description?
options: A palace and a university only
A public bath, drainage system and granary
A temple tower and a stadium
An airport and a railway station
data.explanation: A public bath, drainage and granary is correct as the associated features. Palace and university only is wrong because it overstates later institutions, while temple tower, stadium, airport and railway station are wrong because they are anachronistic.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The Indus script of the Harappan civilisation is what, as of the latest research?
options: Fully deciphered and accepted
Remains undeciphered
Deciphered only in Odisha
Proven to be English
data.explanation: Remains undeciphered is correct as the research position. Fully deciphered is wrong because no accepted decipherment exists, while Odisha-only and English claims are wrong because they invent a decipherment.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Why is the civilisation called Harappan?
options: Because Mohenjo-Daro was its largest city
Because the script was deciphered at Harappa
Because Harappa was the first site that brought it to light
Because it covered only the Harappa region
data.explanation: Harappa as the first site to bring the civilisation to light is correct; Charles Masson reported its remains in 1826. The Mohenjo-Daro option is wrong because the name does not come from Mohenjo-Daro and it was not the largest site; decipherment is wrong because the script is undeciphered; and 'only the Harappa region' is wrong because more than a thousand sites are known.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which statement about Mohenjo-Daro and UNESCO is correct?
options: It was excavated from 1980 and inscribed in 1922
It was unplanned and built of a single brick type
It was inscribed in 1980 after excavations from 1922
It was inscribed in 1826 as World Heritage
data.explanation: Inscribed in 1980 after excavations from 1922 is correct. The reversed dates swap excavation and inscription; the unplanned, single-brick option contradicts the grid layout and the mixed baked and sun-dried brick evidence; and 1826 is when Harappa's remains were reported, not a UNESCO year.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The 2025 OPSC item on the language of the Indus Valley Civilisation tests what?
options: A settled decipherment of the script
A single proven cause of decline
Recognition of unsettled language hypotheses including Dravidian proposals
The exact population of Mohenjo-Daro
data.explanation: Recognition of unsettled hypotheses is correct because the match pairs Dravidian and other proposals. Settled decipherment is wrong because none exists, a proven decline cause is wrong because decline remains debated, and exact population is wrong because it is not the focus of that item.
data.label: pyq-pattern

data.stem: Consider the statements: 1. The civilisation spans many sites. 2. It is named after the single site of Mohenjo-Daro. Which is correct?
options: 2 only
Neither 1 nor 2
1 only
Both 1 and 2
data.explanation: 1 only is correct because the civilisation spans many sites while the name comes from Harappa. The option with 2 only and both are wrong because they misattribute the name to Mohenjo-Daro, while neither is wrong because the first statement is correct.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which statement about Odisha and the Harappan civilisation is supported by NCERT's distribution of Harappan sites?
options: Odisha was the Harappan core with the largest cities
The Mahanadi valley was an established Harappan trade corridor to Mesopotamia
Odisha does not appear among the regions NCERT lists for Harappan finds
Mohenjo-Daro lies in Odisha
data.explanation: Odisha's absence from NCERT's list of regions with Harappan finds is correct. 'Harappan core' is wrong because the core lay in the Indus region and the north-west; the Mahanadi-Mesopotamia corridor is wrong because no cited official source establishes it; and Mohenjo-Daro lies in Sind, Pakistan.
data.label: practice

data.stem: NCERT gives Mohenjo-Daro an approximate area of 125 hectares, while UNESCO gives 240 hectares. Why do the figures differ?
options: UNESCO's 240 hectares measures the inscribed World Heritage property, a different boundary
One of the two figures must be a misprint
The city doubled in size after 1980
125 hectares refers to Harappa, not Mohenjo-Daro
data.explanation: The two figures measure different boundaries: NCERT's describes the settlement, UNESCO's the inscribed property. 'Misprint' is wrong because both are stated deliberately; growth after 1980 is wrong because it is an ancient ruin; and the Harappa option is wrong because NCERT gives the figure for Mohenjo-Daro.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which comparison of Harappa and Mohenjo-Daro is correct?
options: Mohenjo-Daro gives the name; Harappa is the largest known site
Both are the same site with different names
Neither belongs to the Harappan civilisation
Harappa gives the name; Mohenjo-Daro is a major planned city; Rakhigarhi is the largest known site
data.explanation: Harappa giving the name, Mohenjo-Daro as a major planned city and Rakhigarhi as the largest known site is correct. The first option is wrong because the name comes from Harappa, not Mohenjo-Daro, and Harappa is not the largest site; the same-site option is wrong because they are two separate cities; and the 'neither' option is wrong because both are core Harappan cities.
data.label: practice

data.stem: An option claims the script is deciphered and Mohenjo-Daro was unplanned. Why is it doubly incorrect?
options: The settlement was planned but the script claim is correct
The script is undeciphered but the planning claim is correct
Both claims are correct as stated
The script is undeciphered and the grid layout shows planning
data.explanation: Undeciphered with planned grid is correct on both points. The first two options are wrong because they accept one false claim, while both-correct is wrong because it accepts two false claims.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which statement about decline is the most defensible for Prelims?
options: A single flood is proven as the cause
A single invasion is proven as the cause
Decline has never been studied
The cause remains debated and should not be stated as certain
data.explanation: The debated-cause statement is correct because decline causation is unsettled. A single flood and a single invasion are wrong because they present one cause as proven, while never studied is wrong because decline has been extensively debated.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A match pairs Harappan features with their correct associations. Which is correct?
options: Excavation 1980 with inscription 1922 and mature dates 1826
Largest known site Mohenjo-Daro with the name taken from Rakhigarhi
Script deciphered with grid layout 1980 and extent ten sites
Mohenjo-Daro with grid layout, public bath, drainage and mixed baked and sun-dried brick
data.explanation: Mohenjo-Daro with grid, bath, drainage and mixed brick is correct. The first option scrambles the excavation (1922), inscription (1980) and 1826 years; the second swaps size and name (Rakhigarhi is the largest site, Harappa gives the name); the third asserts a decipherment and a wrong extent.
data.label: practice
